metadata.title: Grade 8 A+++ National High-Rigor 36-Week Curriculum
metadata.curriculum_note: There is no single federally mandated national Grade 7 or Grade 8 curriculum. This is a high-rigor synthesis of national frameworks and selected state-level expectations, with added transfer, evidence, modeling, research, and interdisciplinary demands.

national_benchmark_research.research_conclusion: The curriculum prioritizes coherent depth rather than simply accelerating into unrelated high-school content. Grade-level standards are mastered deeply, then extended through unfamiliar-context transfer and interdisciplinary tasks.

weeks.title: Real Numbers & Irrationality
weeks.weekly_objective: Develop deep, transferable Grade 8 mastery of real numbers & irrationality through reasoning, evidence, communication, and application.

lessons.title: Rational vs Irrational
objectives: Master the Grade 8 concept represented by rational vs irrational through conceptual reasoning.
Apply the concept to an unfamiliar problem using precise vocabulary, representations, data, or textual evidence.
Explain, defend, critique, and revise the reasoning rather than relying on answer-only work.
activities: Activate prior knowledge and build a conceptual model.
Study a worked example, then analyze an unfamiliar case.
Complete an independent multistep task with written reasoning.
Use peer or teacher critique to identify an error, assumption, or limitation.
Produce a concise evidence-based explanation.
lessons.assessment: Performance task, written reasoning, and mastery evidence.
lessons.extension: Compare two solution methods, evaluate assumptions, and design a new problem.

performance_task.title: National Scholar Evidence-to-Action Capstone
performance_task.prompt: Investigate a teacher-approved real-world problem. Formulate a researchable question; evaluate credible sources; analyze data; apply mathematics; explain a relevant scientific, historical, civic, or economic system; develop criteria and constraints; design a solution or recommendation; create a visual/model/prototype; write an evidence-based argument with a counterclaim; present and defend the work; and reflect on limitations and next steps.

final_test.mastery_rule: 80%+ overall recommended; no major domain below 70%; A+++ distinction at 90%+ plus successful capstone defense.
